questions.explain: params builds the URL's query string (e.g. ?q=python) for a GET request, including proper encoding of special characters, rather than requiring you to build that string by hand.

questions.q: What is the difference between the `params` and `json` arguments to a `requests` call?
options: params builds the URL's query string; json serializes a dict as the request body (commonly used with POST)
They are interchangeable and do the exact same thing
json only works with GET requests, never POST
params sends data in the request body; json builds the URL
questions.explain: params and json send data to two different places in an HTTP request — the URL's query string versus the request body — which is why mixing them up is a common source of bugs.

questions.q: What does passing a dict to `json=` in a POST request do, beyond sending the data?
options: It prevents the request from ever failing
It automatically serializes the dict and sets the Content-Type header to indicate a JSON body
It converts the request into a GET request
It encrypts the request body
questions.explain: requests' json= parameter both serializes your Python dict into a JSON string for the body and sets the Content-Type: application/json header for you automatically.

questions.q: Why should you always pass a `timeout` value to a `requests` call?
options: timeout is required syntax; requests will not run without it
timeout speeds up every request automatically
Without a timeout, a request that never receives a response can hang the program indefinitely
It is only relevant for POST requests, never GET
questions.explain: Without a timeout, your program will wait forever for a response if the server never replies. Setting a reasonable timeout (e.g. 10 seconds) ensures your code can detect and handle that situation instead of hanging.

questions.q: What is the `headers` parameter in a `requests` call typically used for?
options: Setting the URL path of the request
Building the request's query string
Specifying which Python version to use
Carrying request metadata, most commonly authentication credentials like an Authorization header
questions.explain: headers is a dictionary of HTTP header name/value pairs, most frequently used to pass authentication (Lesson 25) and content negotiation (like Accept) information to the server.
